threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus timetable is a suggestion, not a cruel joke. You’ll learn the route by heart soon enough.
Last night on the N35, a guy tried to sell a rubber chicken like it was street art. The driver just shook his head and kept driving. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stumbled into a hidden yard sale on a Sunday morning, haggling over vintage records while kids played by with old roller skates.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip a beer while watching an impromptu breakdance battle at a bus stop – it's like performance art meets public transport.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid the 14 Mission after 5 PM; it’s like riding a rollercoaster of delays and cranky commuters.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a saxophone in the back of a crowded bus—he started a spontaneous sing-along. Only in the Mission, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars in Gràcia close early, but the hidden corners open up after midnight, full of locals and unlit ambiance.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival in Gràcia by their tendency to order 'café con leche' and then stare blankly when the barista only responds in Catalan.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver shouts 'next stop, Clapton' like it's a riddle instead of directions. Classic rookie move.
Last night on the 196, saw a guy serenading a couple with a ukulele. Best free concert ever, but the couple looked mortified.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw my neighbor's pet chicken roaming the street while I was waiting for the bus – that's when I knew Neukölln had truly claimed me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that doubles as a gallery and hosts poetry nights. Where else can you munch on döner while soaking in art?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they swap out their BART plans for a 10-minute walk after hearing about last night's Civic Center chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 at almost midnight last night—driver cracked jokes with riders while navigating Tenderloin's potholes. That's the spirit!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think the fountains in Plaça del Sol are for decoration, not realizing locals fill their water bottles there daily. It’s a community staple.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their bewilderment at 'tapas' time—dining at 6 PM and expecting it to be full. Just a few locals there, enjoying the quiet.
